tasks.gr8-indigenous-technology-and-processing: Topic: Indigenous technology and processing. Cover preserving metals, galvanising, painting, electroplating, food preservation, local knowledge systems, and sustainability choices. Ask Grade 8 learners to compare methods, explain process purposes, and justify context-appropriate technology decisions.
tasks.gr8-systems-consolidation-and-exam-prepa: Topic: Systems consolidation and exam preparation. Cover integrated revision of mechanical, structural, and electrical vocabulary, mixed diagrams, design communication, and PAT reflection skills. Ask Grade 8 learners to interpret cross-system questions and choose concise, accurate exam responses.
tasks.gr8-cells-batteries-solar-t4: Topic: Electrochemical and solar cells. Cover input devices (electrochemical cell, generator, solar panel), the chemical-to-electrical energy change in a cell and homemade fruit, vegetable and salt-water batteries (a small voltage), identical 1,5 V cells in series (the voltages add: 3 cells give 4,5 V) and in parallel (the voltage stays 1,5 V but the battery lasts longer), and photovoltaic cells with advantages (renewable, no fuel burned) and disadvantages (only when the sun shines, cost). Ask Grade 8 learners to compute series voltages and to weigh advantages and disadvantages.
tasks.gr8-electricity-generation-grid-t4: Topic: Generating electricity and the national grid. Cover thermal power stations (steam turbines; coal, gas, nuclear and the sun as heat sources), hydroelectric power stations including pumped storage, wind-driven turbines, the advantages and disadvantages of each, alternating current, step-up and step-down transformers and the stages of the national grid, and the impact and bias issues: energy for heating, lighting and cooking in rural and informal settlements, illegal connections (ethical and safety issues) and equitable sharing of resources. No transformer calculations. Ask Grade 8 learners to describe, compare and write balanced answers.
tasks.gr8-resistors-ohm-logic-t4: Topic: Resistors, Ohm's law and logic gates. Cover circuit components and accepted symbols (input, output and control devices, short circuits), resistors in series (current decreases) and in parallel (total current increases), Ohm's law QUALITATIVELY with NO calculations (more cells in series give more voltage and, if the resistance is unchanged, more current), AND logic (switches in series) and OR logic (switches in parallel) with truth tables, and a panic button system using OR. Do NOT use V = IR calculations. Ask Grade 8 learners to read truth tables and choose the gate.
